youtube.baslik: How does a surgeon sense facial nerve stress without seeing the screen? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In surgery, the facial nerve is monitored with fine needle electrodes placed in the facial muscles, that is, with electromyography (EMG), and the EMG signal is also sent to a loudspeaker, so the surgeon hears discharges instantly without looking at the screen. A short single discharge when the nerve is touched is often harmless; regular trains of discharges lasting for seconds suggest the nerve is under serious stress.
